page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and utilizing a KVM hypervisor. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by stress-ng single-core CPU and single-threaded gzip compression tests falling into the bottom 25%. However, the instance demonstrates average multi-core efficiency, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all ranking in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is also average, delivering 109.69 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 47.96 GB/sec for uncached large block writes.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c6.8xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution without resource contention. This configuration is well-suited for multi-threaded processing tasks, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations, where parallel execution can offset the lower single-core performance.
